note: Numbers a shop or a guide has set. These always win over anything the engine derives. A derived number is a good default from measured record; a number someone who fishes the water chose is better, and nothing computed may quietly replace it. Add a water here at onboarding and the next scrape keeps what is written rather than overwriting it.

fields.flow.min / flow.max: the scale the bar and sparkline draw against. Derived from USGS daily statistics when absent.
fields.flow.threshold / flow.thresholdLabel: the high-water mark. DERIVED since 2026-09-08: the flow this river exceeds only a tenth of its own April-October record, which fires 21-22 days a season on every water. Six hand-set numbers measured out at anywhere from the 35th to the 93rd percentile of their own rivers, so they were six different rules wearing one label. Set a number here and it still wins -- but write down why, because it will disagree with every other water on the card.
fields.sections: named reaches the pack can be shaped to.
fields.packName: the shop's own name for the pack.
fields.cdecStation: CDEC station id for water temperature (sensor 25, hourly), where USGS does not report 00010. Read through the widget's temp proxy, never from the browser: CDEC sends no CORS header.
fields.reportFreshness: how many days a report stays CURRENT and then RECENT before it reads OLDER, e.g. {"current": 14, "recent": 30}. Never derived. The shop knows how often it updates a water; the card defaults to 14/30 as an INTERIM until they say, and that default is a placeholder, not a standard.
fields.cdecFlow: {station, sensor} for a water's FLOW where USGS carries none. Read through the widget's cdec proxy, never from the browser: CDEC sends no CORS header. The McCloud is the case that found this -- 25 USGS sites carry its name and not one reports a real-time or recent daily series, while CDEC's MCA at Ah-Di-Na reports hourly.

lower-sacramento.why: The scale is hand-set and only the scale. 0-20,000 puts the derived high-water mark at 65% of the bar (13,000 since the 1.5x-median floor, 2026-09-18; 70% before it) and the season's median flow at 44% of it. The pure derivation gives 0-30,000, which is right about storms and pushes the season a reader actually fishes into the bottom third. The threshold itself is derived like every other water's. sections and packName were removed 2026-09-16, when this river joined the weekly scrape: they drive pack building, which needs a sections field on every pick that only a person can assign, and a scraped pick has none -- the resolver crashes rather than guessing. Restore them only alongside hand-authored picks.
lower-sacramento.thresholdWhy: Set 2026-10-06 from The Fly Shop's own Lower Sac report: 'good wading opportunities when the flows are below 7,500 CFS'. A guide's number, so it wins over the derived high-water mark (none was derived here). 7,500 sits at 37.5% of the 0-20,000 scale.
lower-sacramento.cdecStationWhy: USGS Keswick (11370500) reports no water temperature. CDEC KWK (Sacramento R at Keswick, sensor 25, hourly) does: 55.8F on 2026-10-06, the steady ~55F tailwater temperature the shop describes.

mccloud.why: USGS has 25 sites on the McCloud and none of them reports flow. CDEC's MCA, at Ah-Di-Na, reports hourly and is the water the shop's report is about. Its record starts in 2020 -- seven seasons, against 52 to 116 years on the USGS waters -- so the high-water mark here rests on far less evidence than the others and the card says so.
